statement: Every odd composite balanced degree d admits an explicit rational two-pair Image witness F_d with R not dividing F_d, no proper-power representation even up to scalar over field extensions, all pure contractions zero and one fixed marker surviving at every even positive moment order.
domain: Every characteristic-zero field; two contraction pairs; balanced degree d means bidegree(d,d), ordinary degree2d.

logical_inputs.location: Sections2 and4, original contraction, Hopf angular functional and Gamma(shape2) radial identity
logical_inputs.exact_application: For a homogeneous bilinear polynomial H of balanced degreeD, E2(H)=(D+1)! Lambda(H(1,x,y,t)); t^2+2xy=1 and Lambda is phase constant term followed by dt/2 on[-1,1].
logical_inputs.qualification: This is the two-complex-Gaussian radial decomposition, not the ternary real Gaussian moment functional.

logical_inputs.exact_application: Elementary image-kernel reduction, polynomial endpoint Taylor divisibility, parity, explicit homogeneous lift, evaluation at R=0 and exact irreducible T multiplicityone.
logical_inputs.qualification: The proof works for every parameter and every moment order; finite checker cases do not supply those quantifiers.

inspected_primary_sources.authors: Arno van den Essen, David Wright, Wenhua Zhao
inspected_primary_sources.title: On the Image Conjecture
inspected_primary_sources.statement: Theorem3.3, attributed there to Zhao Theorem3.1: the image of the commuting operators xi_i-partial_zi equals the kernel of monomial contraction E.
inspected_primary_sources.inspection: Actual Section3 statement inspected. Opposite signs give the same image subspace. The characteristic-zero field argument needed here is also proved directly in the new note.

inspected_primary_sources.authors: NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
inspected_primary_sources.title: Euler beta integral
inspected_primary_sources.inspection: Actual formula and parameter hypotheses inspected; the degree-nine even-m specialization has a=(m+1)/2,b=m+1. The rational product also follows by finite polynomial integration.

inspected_primary_sources.title: Counterexamples to the xz-Conjecture and the Mathieu Conjecture for SU(2)
inspected_primary_sources.statement: Theorem2.1 gives a mixed interval/torus counterexample with a fixed multiplier surviving at every positive power; Theorem4.2 gives its regular SU(2) lift.
inspected_primary_sources.inspection: Actual displayed formulas, beta-binomial proof and SU(2) integration formula inspected.
inspected_primary_sources.role: Antecedent and priority boundary, not an indispensable proof input to the new odd-composite construction. No claim that unrestricted Mathieu/Image failure or beta cancellation is new.

closest_retained_results: HOPF_LIFT_CLASSIFICATION.md Section7 classifies real signed-height profiles with one affine dilation t(1+x); the new dilation is t(1+x)^(2r), outside that stated class.

TWO_PAIR_IMAGE_MATHIEU_COUNTEREXAMPLE.md Theorem5.5 supplies every even primitive balanced degree>=4; Theorem5.6 excludes complex bilinear multiples of the retained quartic as primitive degree-five witnesses. Those scopes are unchanged.

verification.method: Standard-library original four-variable balanced monomial convolution and factorial contraction, separately compared with exact univariate angular/endpoint identities. No inverse-shear code or assumed universal cutoff is used.
verification.internal_review: Parent independently reconstructed the nonlinear-height all-order proof, degree/marker exponents, R=0 reduction and exact T multiplicity; separately expanded the original four-variable F9 and checked pure/marked contractions through m4. This is internal mathematical review, not external human review.

remaining_scope: This odd-composite family has no prime-degree conclusion of its own. The separate hyperbolic inverse-cover family supplies some odd prime degrees, including13 and23; degrees5 and7 remain open. Nine is only the first odd degree in this family, not a minimum theorem.
The least degree of a bad original marker for arbitrary phases is not classified.
No complete classification of pure two-pair phases, formal verification, external human review or worldwide historical priority is asserted.
